headline: Barret Zoph exits OpenAI again after just five months as enterprise AI sales head
summary: Barret Zoph, who rejoined OpenAI in January to lead enterprise AI sales, has departed the company for the second time in five months. His previous departure from Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab was due to alleged misconduct.
details: Barret Zoph, OpenAI's head of enterprise AI sales, has departed the company for the second time, just five months after rejoining in January 2026. His role was significant as OpenAI aimed to focus on key revenue drivers like enterprise ahead of a planned IPO.

Zoph originally left OpenAI in the fall of 2024 to co-found Thinking Machines Lab with former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati. He abruptly left that role in January 2026 amid reports of alleged misconduct involving an undisclosed relationship with a colleague.

He returned to OpenAI in mid-January 2026, alongside two other former employees who had also left for Thinking Machines Lab. OpenAI's CEO of Applications, Fidji Simo, publicly welcomed them back at the time.
OpenAI has confirmed Zoph's latest departure to The Verge, and Zoph posted a goodbye message in the company's internal Slack channels. He did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The situation adds to existing tensions between OpenAI and Thinking Machines Lab. Mira Murati briefly served as OpenAI's interim CEO during Sam Altman's ouster in November 2023 and testified against Altman in a recent trial.

headline_marked: [[Datasette Apps host custom HTML+JS apps]] with sandboxed SQL queries
headline: Datasette Apps host custom HTML+JS apps with sandboxed SQL queries
summary: Datasette Apps enable embedding self-contained HTML+JavaScript applications directly within Datasette, allowing them to run read-only or configured write SQL queries against your data in a tightly secured iframe sandbox.
details: Datasette has launched 'Datasette Apps', a new plugin allowing users to host custom HTML+JavaScript applications directly within their Datasette instances. These apps run in a tightly constrained <iframe> sandbox, providing a secure environment for custom functionality.

The sandboxed environment prevents apps from accessing cookies or localStorage and includes an injected Content Security Policy (CSP) header. This design prevents malicious or buggy applications from exfiltrating private data or making unauthorized HTTP requests to external hosts.

Apps can execute read-only SQL queries against Datasette data using JavaScript. For write operations, they can be configured with specific stored queries, ensuring controlled data modification within the secure sandbox.

The project evolved from an attempt to build a Claude Artifacts mechanism for Datasette Agent, recognizing the broader potential of sandboxed applications. This approach transforms custom HTML tools into a core feature of the Datasette ecosystem.

A key innovation is the combination of <iframe> sandbox attributes with an immutable <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"> header. This dual-layer security ensures untrusted code cannot interact with the parent application or bypass security policies.

Communication between the sandboxed app and Datasette is managed via a MessageChannel()-based transport. This allows allow-listed SQL queries to be safely executed by the parent Datasette instance after verification, enhancing defense in depth.
